_comment: Provenance for WASM bundles built from the pqctoday-hsm repo and vendored into this hub. When you rebuild a bundle with its hsm build script, update its `hsmCommit`/`builtAt`. Verify drift with `npm run sync:wasm:check` (compares against a sibling ../pqctoday-hsm checkout when present; no-op otherwise). Bundles built from other sources (openssl upstream, pqctoday-tpm) are intentionally omitted.

bundles.name: cacp-kmip
bundles._priorBuildNote20260813: Rebuilt 2026-08-13 from hsm main @ d9b3f42 via scripts/build-kmip-wasm.sh, after the KMIP 3.0 item-10 stack merged (#166/#167/#168/#169): Baseline Server profile is now 13/13, with all five server-to-client operations implemented, and the OASIS corpus carries machine-checked provenance against the CSD02 zip. The restage also uncovered that the wasm target had not compiled since #166 — server/secp384r1mlkem1024.rs uses rustls without the native-only cfg gate its neighbour listener.rs already carries — fixed in hsm #170. This bundle is built from the tree WITH that fix, which is why the recorded commit is #170's merge rather than #169's — at 8ffdd1f the wasm target does not compile at all, so no artifact can correspond to it. #170 also adds a wasm32 type-check to the local gate so the next such break is caught by the gate rather than by the next person to restage. Verified by the build's own smoke suite running IN wasm, not by exit code: ML-DSA-65 CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify round trip (3309-byte signature, Valid), Falcon-512 correctly rejected with the keystore unchanged, and an X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round trip. 144 corpus tests staged (mandatory=95, optional=7, pqc=42).
bundles._buildNote:
Rebuilt 2026-08-14 from hsm main @ fd2c902 (v0.23.0) via scripts/build-kmip-wasm.sh, from the same pristine `git archive v0.23.0` extraction as softhsmrustv3-engine.

READ THIS BEFORE JUDGING THE PREVIOUS GAP: this bundle sat 15 commits stale, and the obvious reading -- that nobody bothered -- is wrong. The wasm target DID NOT COMPILE from #166 until d9b3f42 ('fix(wasm): the wasm target has not compiled since #166 -- gate the rustls module'). d9b3f42 is WHY this bundle is buildable again at all. Anyone looking at the drift count alone would assume it was buildable the whole time and wonder why it was left; it wasn't.

HUB was set explicitly to this worktree. The script's default target is $ROOT/../pqctoday-hub, which is a DIFFERENT agent's active worktree -- letting it default would have written this bundle into someone else's tree.

VERIFIED BY ARTIFACT, not exit code. sha256 34f05fd8... -> a58f6cd8..., size 5543719 bytes. Both tracked copies (public/wasm/rust-kmip/ and src/wasm/kmip/) hash-checked equal. The build's own node smoke suite PASSED in wasm, through the hybrid-KEM encapsulate/decapsulate round trip.

CORPUS STAGING CONFIRMED TO HAVE RUN -- this step has gone missing from copies of this script before, and a stale corpus replaying against a fresh engine looks identical to a synced one. public/kmip-corpus/manifest.json regenerated: 144 tests (mandatory=95, optional=7, pqc=42), and section61-headings.json + tags-enums.json were re-staged from the v0.23.0 spec dir.

MANIFEST hsmCommit WAS HAND-CORRECTED, deliberately: the staging step derives it from `git -C $ROOT rev-parse HEAD`, and a `git archive` extraction has no .git, so it wrote the literal string 'unknown'. src/wasm/kmip/corpus/runner.local.test.ts asserts the manifest's hsmCommit prefix-matches THIS bundle's, so 'unknown' would have failed that gate. Set to fd2c9024fd4465ce8dd48b74b7541ffad17abc28, the commit actually extracted and built.

bundles.name: softhsmrustv3-engine
bundles._priorBuildNote20260808: Rebuilt 2026-08-08 from hsm main @ 3480bec (v0.21.0) via rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh, closing a 6-commit drift over rust/. No functional change reachable from this target: the v0.21.0 rust/ work is the operation-evidence log, and its sink is cfg-gated OUT on wasm32-unknown-unknown (see the 'WASM targets must keep building' note in rust/src/oplog.rs), which is why no PQCEV string appears in the bundl
bundles._priorBuildNote20260813main: Rebuilt 2026-08-13 from hsm main @ d9b3f42 and the output was BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previous bundle (sha256 310d3a911b62e66bd1a1beaefcd641b835183cc7c1377960fbe03112485982a7) — which is precisely why it is worth recording. The sibling openssl-pkcs11 bundle had shipped four days of stale bytes because its build path consumes a prebuilt archive; this one runs cargo directly, so it had already picked up hsm d07dfa9 (RSA private keys expose CKA_MODULUS/CKA_PUBLIC_EXPONENT). Established by rebuilding and comparing digests, NOT by trusting the build timestamp — 'the bundle was built after the fix landed' is exactly the reasoning that proved wrong for openssl-pkcs11. Re-anchor only; no behaviour change.
bundles._buildNote: Rebuilt 2026-08-14 from hsm main @ 38affc078, which includes the wasm-target fix (#173): #172 had referenced crate::ck_abi from handlers.rs, and ck_abi is cfg'd out on wasm32-unknown-unknown, so the browser target did not compile at all. CI passed regardless because CI does not build that target. Both prebuilt inputs were rebuilt first, in order — the wasm32-unknown-emscripten staticlib, then libpkcs11-provider.a with FORCE=1 (the script silently skips with exit 0 otherwise) — and the script's own 'archive built BEFORE HEAD' warning was absent on this run.

bundles._priorBuildNote20260812:
Rebuilt 2026-08-12 from hsm main @ 132b6b7 via scripts/build-wasm.sh with emsdk 6.0.4 (SKIP_OPENSSL=1 -- deps/openssl-wasm untouched), closing a 1-commit drift over src/lib. The drift was REAL, not the false-drift pattern the softhsmrustv3-engine note warns about: 20150b0 (#162, 'X-Wing on the Rust engine') also changed the C++ engine -- src/lib/SoftHSM_keygen.cpp +76/-3 and src/lib/SoftHSM_slots.cpp +4 -- so the diff was checked before spending the build, exactly as that note instructs.

BUILT IN DOCKER, not on the host: no emscripten toolchain is installed on this machine any more (the 2026-08-10 build's CMakeCache still held /Users/... paths). Used the official emscripten/emsdk:6.0.4 image, the same toolchain version the last two builds recorded, so the codegen baseline is unchanged. The stale host CMakeCache had to be removed first -- cmake refuses a cache whose source dir differs from the container's /src, and the run reported DOCKER EXIT 0 while having built nothing, which is why the artifacts were checked rather than the exit code.

VERIFIED BY ARTIFACT: node tests/smoke-wasm.mjs PASSED against this exact binary (through C_Logout / C_CloseSession / C_Finalize). The two .wasm are byte-identical to each other (single sha256 across both), as before. Export surface unchanged, compared LIKE-FOR-LIKE against the binary being replaced rather than against a remembered number: 93 distinct C_* symbols in both, with an empty symmetric difference. Size 2387003 -> 2385751 bytes.

GLUE WAS NOT STALE -- a claim I made and then disproved, recorded so nobody re-investigates it. public/wasm/softhsm.js is 139290 bytes while this build emits 91013, and the 2026-08-10 note reads 'the glue shrank 139290 -> 91013 bytes on the newer emsdk', which together look exactly like a shipped glue left behind by a .wasm-only copy. It is a formatting artifact: the hub's pre-commit hook runs prettier over public/wasm/*.js, so the committed glue is the EXPANDED form of the raw emitted file. Prettifying this build's 91013-byte output with the repo's own config yields 139290 bytes BYTE-IDENTICAL to the file already shipped. The glue and the binary have matched all along, and the 2026-08-10 note compared a prettified committed file against a raw build output -- not like for like. Only the two .wasm changed in this commit; the .js are unchanged because they had nothing to change to.
bundles._priorBuildNote20260813:
Rebuilt 2026-08-13 from the PKCS#11 v3.2 conformance branch fix/pkcs11-v32-audit-remediation-0813 @ 9a5794e via scripts/build-wasm.sh with emsdk 6.0.4, SKIP_OPENSSL=1. THIS COMMIT IS LOCAL-ONLY AND UNPUSHED -- see the softhsmrustv3-engine note above; re-pin when it lands.

BUILT ON THE HOST, NOT IN DOCKER. The 2026-08-12 note on this entry says 'no emscripten toolchain is installed on this machine any more'. That is STALE and was the reason a whole conformance branch sat unreachable from the playground: emsdk 6.0.4 is fully present at /Users/pqctoday/Antigravity/emsdk (emcc --version verified 6.0.4, fe5be6af), it is simply not on PATH. `source emsdk_env.sh` is the whole fix.

VERIFIED BY ARTIFACT, not exit code. sha256 c24bb653... -> de8b6484..., size 2385751 -> 2401433 bytes. The two shipped .wasm remain byte-identical to each other (single sha256 across softhsm.wasm and libsofthsmv3.wasm), as in every prior build. Export surface compared like-for-like via WebAssembly.Module.exports: 110 exports both sides, empty symmetric difference. node tests/smoke-wasm.mjs PASSED against this exact binary, through the ML-KEM-768 encapsulate/decapsulate round trip (shared secrets matched, 32 bytes) and on to C_Logout / C_CloseSession / C_Finalize.

This build is what makes the v3.2 conformance work reach a visitor. The behaviour that changed and is now live in the browser includes: XMSS/XMSS-MT keygen takes its parameter set from CKA_PARAMETER_SET in the public template ONLY (v3.2 6.66.6, 'This mechanism does not have a parameter') and returns CKR_TEMPLATE_INCOMPLETE when it is absent instead of silently issuing a 10_256 key; HBS private keys are forced CKA_SENSITIVE=TRUE / CKA_EXTRACTABLE=FALSE (plus CKA_COPYABLE=FALSE for HSS) and a template contradicting that is CKR_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID; ECDH-as-KEM ciphertext is raw, not DER-wrapped.

The .js glue IS regenerated here (91013 bytes raw). The committed form is the prettier-expanded one the repo's pre-commit hook produces -- see the 2026-08-12 note, which already disproved the 'stale glue' theory.

bundles.name: openssl-pkcs11
bundles._rebuild20260813: Rebuilt 2026-08-13 from hsm main @ d9b3f42, and the reason matters more than the rebuild. The 2026-08-09 entry below reasoned that rust/ had 'no real input change — only rust/bench-harness moved', and so relinked openssl.wasm without rebuilding libsofthsmrustv3.a. That reasoning was wrong: hsm d07dfa9 (2026-08-09 17:28) had changed rust/src/ffi.rs to expose CKA_MODULUS and CKA_PUBLIC_EXPONENT on RSA private keys, without which pkcs11-provider's fetch_rsa_key() fails its required fetch, never populates the optional CKA_ID, and reports the misleading 'No CKA_ID in source object'. The bundle was linked at 21:42 that evening — four hours after the fix — from an archive built Aug 8 23:42, the day before it. Both recorded commits (1cab535, dc9c0a838) genuinely contain the fix, so provenance read 'current' the entire time while the shipped bytes did not have it, and e2e/cms-workshop-crypto.spec.ts:392 (LAMPS composite id-MLDSA44-RSA2048-PSS-SHA256) failed nightly from 2026-08-09 to 2026-08-13. Only the RSA profile failed; the ECDSA profiles passed, because an EC or ML-DSA public key is derivable from its private key and the provider never needs to resolve a sibling object. This rebuild deletes both input archives first so a skipped rebuild cannot hide, then rebuilds libsofthsmrustv3.a (cargo rustc --release --target wasm32-unknown-emscripten, confirmed by a 'Compiling softhsmrustv3' line and a changed size) and libpkcs11-provider.a before relinking. build-wasm.sh now also writes public/wasm/openssl-link-inputs.json recording the SHA-256 of every archive it links, because a commit comparison cannot see a stale intermediate and this one went unseen for four days.
bundles._rebuild20260807: Rebuilt 2026-08-07 from hsm main @ 67f739f (merge of PR #153, feat/rust-pkcs11-emscripten-staticlib), closing a 3-commit drift — the same feature branch this bundle's _priorBuild/_buildNote below already describe now landed on main via a clean merge (hsm main's rust/ tree after the merge is identical to 859774b's, confirmed via `git log --stat`). NOTE: the hsmCommit given in the original task request (67f739fc3916b08fe59445120d93f26dfd79d639) does not exist in the hsm repo — corrected here to the actual merge-commit HEAD (67f739fc331cfdb1406197583cf6432f52833080), verified via `git rev-parse HEAD` in pqctoday-hsm. Rebuilt fresh end-to-end per the established process: scripts/build-pkcs11-provider-wasm.sh prerequisite (idempotent — archive already current), a fresh wasm32-unknown-emscripten Rust staticlib build with --features acvp (superseding the stale 2026-07-24 archive), OpenSSL 3.6.3 source re-verified against the pinned sha256 (243a86649cf6f23eeb6a2ff2456e09e5d77dd9018a54d3d96b0c6bdd6ba6c7f1) before extracting, then pqctoday-priv/build-wasm.sh with HUB_ROOT/HSM_ROOT/OPENSSL_SRC set explicitly. Since the underlying rust/ tree is unchanged from the last build, the resulting binary is FUNCTIONALLY IDENTICAL to the previous one — this rebuild is provenance/timestamp hygiene, not a behavior change. VERIFIED: `openssl version` reports 3.6.3; all custom exports present (_pqctoday_cms_init, _pqctoday_composite_mkcert, _execute_cmp_simulation, PKCS#11 C_* symbols); 17/17 real ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/ML-KEM cross-implementation KATs (Node 24 crypto vs this WASM binary) pass; 72/72 in the rest of the OpenSSL Studio + anchor-KAT suites (89 total, 0 failed); `npx tsc -b` clean.
bundles._rebuild20260802: Rebuilt 2026-08-02 from hsm main @ 8386717 (v0.20.2), closing a 6-commit drift AND moving the bundled OpenSSL from 3.6.2 to 3.6.3 (deliberate, user-approved — hsm's deps/openssl-wasm had already moved to 3.6.3 in v0.19.0, so the bundle was behind on both axes). Source: openssl-3.6.3.tar.gz from the official GitHub release, sha256 verified against the published checksum (243a86649cf6f23eeb6a2ff2456e09e5d77dd9018a54d3d96b0c6bdd6ba6c7f1) before extracting. Build needs a prerequisite the main script does not build itself: scripts/build-pkcs11-provider-wasm.sh must run first to produce build-wasm/lib/libpkcs11-provider.a, otherwise build-wasm.sh exits immediately with 'missing pkcs11-provider archive'. Invoked as: HUB_ROOT=<hub checkout> HSM_ROOT=<hsm> OPENSSL_SRC=<openssl-3.6.3 tree> bash pqctoday-priv/build-wasm.sh (HUB_ROOT must be set explicitly — the script's location-derived default is wrong since it moved into pqctoday-priv). The 'apps/openssl link failed (undefined symbol: pqctoday_cms_init)' line in the log is EXPECTED and handled — the script continues to its own custom emcc link; do not read it as a build failure. VERIFIED: `openssl version` now reports 3.6.3 (via the real driver harness, not assumed); OpenSSL Studio suites 57/57 main + 32/32 local incl. the ML-DSA/ML-KEM cross-implementation and anchor KATs, all of which re-confirm real crypto outputs against this new binary; and — closing the prior entry's explicit 'NOT YET VERIFIED: a full pass in an actual browser' gap — e2e/cms-hsm-sign.spec.ts 5/5 in real chromium, including T3 routing an ML-DSA-65 CMS signature through pkcs11-provider into softhsmv3 with 'HSM (pkcs11:)' / 'resident in softhsmv3' evidence. Version references across the Studio's UI copy, lessons, glossary and KAT comments were updated 3.6.2 -> 3.6.3; the only 3.6.2 mentions left are dated historical records of when content was first captured. STILL UNCONFIRMED (carried over): whether the 'HRR detection' patch referenced by the build script's banner is present in this tree.
